title: fix(schema-catalog): icon-sizes authors pixels, so the four icons differ (objectui#7565)
body:
Fixes #7565

`IconSchema.size` is declared `size?: number` — pixels, `@default 24`
(`packages/types/src/layout.ts:196`). The fixture authored `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`.
`IconRenderer` builds `sizeStyle = { width: schema.size, height: schema.size }`
(`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/icon.tsx:115`), so each string went straight
into `style.width`, the CSSOM dropped it as an invalid length, and all four icons fell
back to lucide's 24. Four pixel values now, chosen to differ visibly, with `24` kept as
the second so the declared default stays on display.

⛔ The t-shirt enum was NOT added to `IconSchema`. Nothing outside the one JSON file is
touched: no `packages/types`, no zod mirror, no renderer, no gate.

## Rendered reading — through the real `SchemaRenderer`, both variants in one run

`render(SchemaRenderer schema=...)` against the gallery registration set, reading each
`svg`'s inline `style` and `getComputedStyle`. Both halves measured in the same run, so
the after-reading is not a walk that stopped finding nodes (`svg` count is 4 in both).

| authored `size` | inline `style` | computed width / height |
|---|---|---|
| `"sm"` | *(none)* | `""` / `""` |
| `"md"` | *(none)* | `""` / `""` |
| `"lg"` | *(none)* | `""` / `""` |
| `"xl"` | *(none)* | `""` / `""` |
| `16` | `width: 16px; height: 16px;` | `16px` / `16px` |
| `24` | `width: 24px; height: 24px;` | `24px` / `24px` |
| `32` | `width: 32px; height: 32px;` | `32px` / `32px` |
| `48` | `width: 48px; height: 48px;` | `48px` / `48px` |

The SVG `width`/`height` **attributes** read `24` in BOTH halves and are not the result:
they are lucide's own numeric `size` prop default, and CSS `width`/`height` win over the
SVG presentation attributes — spelled out in `icon.tsx`'s own docblock (lines 89-92).
The inline style is the channel the authored size travels on, and it is empty in all four
rows above the rule and distinct in all four below it.

## ⭐ Why `safeValidateSchema` did not refuse the string — none of the three candidates

The dispatch offered three: (1) the fixture is not reached, (2) the zod mirror disagrees
with the TypeScript declaration, (3) it is already in the known-failing bucket of
`examples/schema-catalog/test/safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts`. **It is none of them.**
Measured on `origin/main` `3f93fe47d`:

```
safeValidateSchema(icon-sizes.json as authored)          -> success: true
safeValidateSchema(icon-sizes.json after this PR)        -> success: true
safeValidateSchema({type:'icon', icon:'star', size:'sm'})-> success: false  (": Invalid input")
safeValidateSchema({type:'icon', icon:'star', size:16})  -> success: true
```

- **Not (1).** The document IS reached and IS parsed — `safeValidateSchema` returns a
  verdict on it, and the verdict is `success`.
- **Not (2).** The mirror agrees with the declaration: `layout.zod.ts:160` says
  `size: z.number().optional().default(24)`, and line 3 above proves it does refuse the
  string when the node is the root.
- **Not (3).** It was never in the failing bucket, so this PR does not shrink it. The
  bucket is `objectui check`'s `unvalidatedCandidates`, reached only when
  `isObjectUiSchemaFile` is FALSE (`packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:134`) — and that
  function is `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS.some(k => k in content) || safeValidateSchema(content).success`.
  This document fails to be a candidate twice over: `children` is the second entry of
  `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` (`check.ts:36`) so the cheap structural arm short-circuits
  before the validity arm runs, and the validity arm would have said `success` anyway.

**The actual mechanism is a fourth one, and it is the reading worth keeping.**
`safeValidateSchema` is `AnyComponentSchema.safeParse` (`zod/index.zod.ts:435`), and
`AnyComponentSchema` — the per-type union — is applied to the **root node only**. A child
is reached through `children` / `body`, both `z.union([SchemaNodeSchema, z.array(SchemaNodeSchema)])`
(`zod/base.zod.ts:141` / `:146`, respelled identically on `FlexSchema`, `layout.zod.ts:206`),
and `SchemaNodeSchema` (`zod/base.zod.ts:53`) is
`z.lazy(() => z.union([BaseSchemaCore, z.string(), z.number(), z.boolean(), z.null(), z.undefined()]))`.
The object arm is `BaseSchemaCore`, **not** `AnyComponentSchema`, and `BaseSchemaCore` ends
`.passthrough()` (`zod/base.zod.ts:241`). So the nested `icon` node was matched against the
generic base object, which declares neither `icon` nor `size`, and both keys passed through
unread. Enforcement of every per-type declaration is root-only, at every depth, for every
component type.

This is **not** the objectui#7444 mechanism. There the key was undeclared and
`.passthrough()` tolerated it. Here the key is declared, correctly, on both faces — and the
child simply never reaches the schema that declares it. It is a dispatch defect, not a
tolerance one. Filed unassigned as objectui#7869 with the full reading; ⛔ not repaired here
(it would move a published validator, Clause-2 `yes`).

## objectui#7860 / objectui#7548 — nothing to edit, as intended

`safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts` is untouched by this PR and its bucket did not move, so
no prose there needed rewriting in either direction. The check the dispatch asked for comes
back clean: this repair required **nobody** to edit that file.

## Verification — all on `ee7f631f5` (this branch's HEAD)

Exit codes captured by redirecting first, never through a pipe. Verdict lines quoted as the
tools printed them.

| what | verdict |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run examples/schema-catalog/` | `Test Files  28 passed (28)` / `Tests  2075 passed (2075)`, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-schema-catalog type-check` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, script name echoed, so not a zero-match run) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6377 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` exit 0 |
| `python3 scripts/regenerate-catalog-index.py --check` | `examples/schema-catalog/src/index.ts is up to date (431 entries).` exit 0 |

⚠️ **The catalog suite is NOT evidence for this repair, and saying so is the point.** It read
`Test Files 28 passed (28)` / `Tests 2075 passed (2075)` on `origin/main` `3f93fe47d` with the
defect present, and reads exactly the same numbers now. It is insensitive in both directions;
the render table above is the evidence, and the suite only shows nothing else moved.

**Changeset:** none owed — the gate's verdict line is quoted above and the diff is one
`examples/` fixture. No `skip-changeset` label applied: in this repo that label is inert
(no workflow or script reads it) and the gate's verdict is the authority.

**Lint narrowing, declared.** `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) was not run whole.
Three readings instead: (1) every `files` entry in `eslint.config.js` is `**/*.{ts,tsx}` —
no block names `.json`; (2) `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the changed file
returns 1 result, `errorCount 0`, and its only message is
`File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied.`; (3) no type-aware linting is
configured (`eslint.config.js` has no `project` / `projectService`), and the diff touches no
`.ts`/`.tsx` and no config, so no untouched file's verdict can move. The diff contains zero
lintable files.

**Not run, stated plainly:** the `objectui check` CLI itself (the bucket claim above is
derived from the measured `safeValidateSchema` verdict plus the two read lines of
`check.ts`, not from a CLI run); the repo-wide `pnpm test`; any browser/visual check beyond
the jsdom render above; the CI gate farm, which will run it once regardless.
